answer: In an agent economy, each participant must stake a unique hardware token that continuously burns a tiny ember of compute power to prove liveness, registered against a shared orchard of verified devices. An attacker spinning up many Sybils would need to buy and power a matching number of physical tokens, making the cost linear with the number of identities rather than free software clones, so a farm of hundreds becomes prohibitively expensive while honest agents share the oasis of trust.
